Oct. 5, 2026

To the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission:

The Sierra Club submits the following 350 digital comments on behalf of our members
and supporters with the following comment, along with 187 personalized messages
(bolded):


Dear Commissioners:

Here in the Southwest, we cannot handle more fossil-fuel infrastructure, including
another methane gas pipeline.
Over the past 20 years, climate impacts have exacerbated a relentless drought that has
left our rivers and arroyos dry, and our communities without the water they need to
survive. The droughts have been especially hard on our farmers. This pipeline project,
along with the power plants and data centers it would support, would further threaten
our rivers, arroyos, and groundwater. The risk to our fragile ecosystems is not worth it.
Similarly, much of our region is already polluted from power plants and other fossil-fuel
infrastructure. Methane leaks are an inevitable outcome of these pipelines and would
further threaten the health and wellbeing of the surrounding communities. Already, we
live with power plants, solid-waste dumps, pipelines, and other polluting infrastructure
that has rendered our air unhealthy to breathe. This pipeline does not serve the people
or our communities. It serves billion-dollar corporations.
The gas in this pipeline and the energy produced at the power plants it will feed do not
serve our need for more secure sources of electricity, nor do they make our electricity
more affordable. If built, this pipeline would be another one of those projects that is all
burden and no benefit for our communities.
Please reject the permit application for this pipeline.
 Fight the gas pipelines that make Project Jupiter & El Paso 1 possible!!!
